name: Saint Stanislaus
history: Bishop of Kraków who rebuked King Bolesław II for his cruelty and his sins, and was killed in 1079, by tradition at the king’s own hand while celebrating Mass. The facts of the quarrel are disputed by historians, but Poland has honoured him for centuries as a martyr for the moral law and as one of her patrons.
life: Stanislaus was born at Szczepanów in southern Poland, studied, perhaps at Gniezno, and was ordained priest. In 1072 he became bishop of Kraków. King Bolesław II, called the Bold, was a capable soldier and ruler, but the bishop came into conflict with him; the later chronicles speak of the king’s cruelty and immorality and of the bishop’s rebukes, ending in excommunication. Tradition holds that Bolesław, unable to find men willing to kill the bishop, struck him down himself in the church on the Skałka in Kraków. A popular legend tells that Stanislaus once raised a dead man, Piotrowin, to testify in a dispute over land. The king was driven into exile soon after. Stanislaus was canonised at Assisi in 1253, and his relics rest in Wawel Cathedral. John Paul II, his successor in Kraków, called him a patron of the moral order.
prayerTo: Saint Stanislaus, shepherd of Kraków, you spoke the truth to a king and paid for it with your life. Pray for bishops and for all who must correct the powerful. Give me courage to speak for what is right, gently and without fear, and to stand by the truth when it costs me. Amen.
penance: Pray today for those in public authority, and for the Church in Poland. If you have been avoiding a necessary word of correction, ask for the grace to give it with charity.
meditation: He was killed, the tradition says, at the altar, in the middle of the Mass. Is there any truth you have kept quiet because speaking it would cost you?
